albums.blurb: Tommy Guerrero made his name in the 1980s as a street-skating pioneer on Powell-Peralta's Bones Brigade before co-founding Real Skateboards — the music came later, recorded at home in San Francisco. This second album, released on James Lavelle's Mo' Wax label (home of DJ Shadow and UNKLE), gathers fourteen short, entirely instrumental sketches for guitar, bass, and drum machine that fold Latin soul, jazz, and dusty hip-hop rhythms into one unhurried haze.
albums.reception: Long out of print after its 2000 Mo' Wax release, it was reissued as a remastered double LP by Be With Records in 2017 and has stayed in demand since, with represses as recent as 2025.

albums.blurb: Josh Tillman drummed for Fleet Foxes and released a string of quiet records as J. Tillman before reinventing himself as Father John Misty. This second album under the name, released on Sub Pop in 2015, is a lush orchestral folk-rock song cycle about meeting and marrying his wife Emma — mariachi horns and strings, one drum-machine detour in "True Affection," and some of his sharpest, most self-lacerating writing.
albums.reception: It debuted at number 17 on the Billboard 200 and holds a Metacritic score of 87 ("universal acclaim"), appearing on more than 70 publications' 2015 year-end lists.

albums.blurb: Sessa is the São Paulo songwriter Sergio Sayeg, who sings in Portuguese over nylon-string guitar, close backing harmonies, and light percussion in a lineage that runs back through Caetano Veloso and 1970s MPB. Estrela Acesa ("burning star"), his second album, released on Mexican Summer in 2022, surrounds that spare foundation with richer arrangements than his 2019 debut Grandeza.
albums.reception: Pitchfork's 7.3 review praised how his "unhurried nylon string guitar and softly danceable rhythms put a smooth, minimalist flourish on the vibrant musical heritage of Brazil."
